messages:
erin: Heads up — after the RBAC policy rollout last night we're seeing a huge SCIM deprovision backlog. Thousands queued, workers stuck on KMS decrypt failures. Anyone seeing this in prod dashboards?
ben: 😬 saw a spike in scim-errors alert at 00:20 UTC. DMed logs to the oncall.
claire: Got a sample? can you paste an error snippet (no PII)
erin: Paste of the worker log:```
2024-04-05T00:19:42Z scim-worker-12 ERROR deprovision failed user=acct-xyz err="KMSDecryptError: InvalidCiphertextException" request_id=abc123
2024-04-05T00:19:42Z scim-worker-12 WARN retries=3 state=pending
```
dave: That's the KMS InvalidCiphertext pattern I saw during the key alias rotation incident earlier. Was there any key alias rotation as part of the rollout?
erin: The RBAC rollout included a key alias rename for the scim-service role (per the rollout notes). It was intended to be a metadata change only, but maybe something touching KMS perms happened.
sam: From security: we changed a resource-based policy to tighten access to the KMS key, so only scim-service role can decrypt now. If workers cached an old key identifier or ran with a different role, they'd start failing.
claire: Repro command from a staging worker (won't decrypt):```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id alias/scim-service-v1 --region us-east-1
# -> An error: InvalidCiphertextException
```
ben: I tried restarting one worker pod and it immediately re-auth'd and resumed deprovisions for that shard. Might be that long-lived processes have a cached CMK id that needs refresh.
dave: Oncall action: restarting scim-workers eu-west-1 and us-east-1 now. deploy-bot: restart job queued (job id 20240405-111)
deploy-bot: restart started for scim-workers (eu-west-1) by dave
kms-bot: detected recent KeyPolicy update on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh, event_ts=1712499900
erin: after EU restart: some workers recovered, errors down 70%. Still ~800 pending in backfill queue.
ben: For a quick mitigation we can: 1) restart all scim-workers to pick up new key metadata, 2) run a controlled backfill throttled to avoid rate limits, 3) add monitoring for InvalidCiphertextException counts.
claire: Agreed. Also adding a small library change to detect KMS InvalidCiphertext and force a key metadata refresh (and fail fast so operator can restart pod) -> quick PR incoming.
erin: Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scim-service/pull/402 (hotfix - kms refresh on decrypt failure)
dave: Restart completed in both regions. Initial metrics show dequeue rate back to baseline 5m ago.
sam: Security note: we verified key policy change was intentional and scoped correctly. No evidence of compromised keys. This was an availability/regression issue.
ben: Follow-up tasks: - Claire to land hotfix and cut canary -> owner: claire - Erin to run a controlled backfill and watch SLOs -> owner: erin - Ops to add alert for KMS InvalidCiphertext spikes -> owner: dave
erin: Started controlled backfill, rate=50/s. Monitoring logs.
claire: Hotfix merged and canary reverted to rollout channel. Will roll to 100% once we confirm stable.
dave: Setting a temporary runbook note: if KMS InvalidCiphertext spikes after a policy rotation, restart the scim-worker fleet and scale down backfill to zero while investigating.
erin: Postmortem notes will include: cause = key policy tighten + long-lived worker cache, mitigation = worker restart + code fix for key metadata refresh, permanent fix = add rotation-aware refresh + test in staging.
sam: Marking as not a security compromise; we'll include timeline for audit log.
ben: Closing thread for now, will reopen if backlog doesn't clear by EOD. :thumbsup:
